title: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This document defines Redwood Inference’s integrated policy for annual and rolling budgeting and forecasting, procurement and contracts lifecycle, and revenue recognition & billing controls. It establishes processes, approval thresholds, ownership, and templates to ensure predictable spend, compliant contracting, timely procurement, and GAAP-aligned revenue recognition. This policy applies to all Redwood business units and legal entities unless an explicit exception is granted by Finance & Legal.

Scope

- Budgeting & Forecasting: annual budgeting cycle, quarterly rolling forecasts, variance management, capital vs. operating classification.
- Procurement & Contracts: requisition-to-pay process, vendor selection, contract intake, negotiation guardrails, signature authorities.
- Revenue Recognition & Billing: invoicing cadence, ASC 606 alignment principles, deferred revenue management, credits/refunds, and billing dispute handling.

Principles

1. Accuracy and timeliness: Budgets and forecasts should reflect realistic plans and be updated promptly for material changes.
2. Control and segregation of duties: Procurement, contracting, and revenue recognition processes must separate requestors, approvers, and accounting/review roles.
3. Minimization of risk: Contract language should protect Redwood’s IP, limit liability, and meet data/security requirements.
4. Compliance with accounting standards: Revenue must be recognized in accordance with ASC 606 / local GAAP as applicable.

Part A — Budgeting and Forecasting

Overview

The Finance team leads an annual budgeting cycle and maintains a continuous rolling 12-month forecast. Product, Engineering, GTM, and Ops provide input through their owners. The goal is to align resource allocation with strategic priorities while maintaining adequate runway and margin targets.

Timeline and Deliverables

1. Annual Budget (October–December)
   - Oct 1: Budget kickoff & guidance published by Finance (assumptions, FX rates, headcount caps).
   - Oct–Nov: Department budget drafts submitted to Finance using the standard budget template (file reference: BudgetTemplate_YYYY.xlsx).
   - Nov 15: Leadership review cycle begins (finance + exec).
   - Dec 15: Board-ready budget submitted to CEO/CFO.

2. Rolling Forecast (monthly cadence)
   - Rolling 12-month forecast updated by Finance on the 10th business day of each month.
   - Material variances (>10% of line item or >$100k) require written variance explanation and corrective plan.

Budgeting Rules and Classifications

- Capital vs Operating: Any spend for hardware, software licenses >$25k and multi-year useful life requires capitalization review with Finance.
- Headcount: All new hires must be approved against the headcount plan; contractor FTE equivalence must be documented.
- Cost Centers: Expenses must be coded to official cost centers; Finance will reject miscoded spend.

Ownership and Decision Rights

- Department Heads: Responsible for draft budgets and headcount plans.
- Finance (Owner): Consolidation, scenario modeling, final budget publication, and variance reporting.
- CFO: Final approver for budget and material reforecasts.

Part B — Procurement and Contracts Process

Procurement Principles

- Competitive sourcing for purchases >$50k annually unless sole-source justification is documented.
- Preferred vendors and corporate agreements must be used where available.
- Procurement decisions must include security/data protection screening for any vendor touching customer data.

Requisition-to-Pay Workflow

1. Requestor: Submit a Purchase Requisition (PR) in the procurement system and attach required approvals and SOW/license details.
2. Manager Approval: Approves budget availability and business justification.
3. Procurement Review: Procurement team validates vendor, pricing, tax, security questionnaire status, and creates PO.
4. Legal Review (if applicable): Contracts team reviews/negotiates terms per Contract Playbook.
5. Finance: Confirms GL coding, payment terms, and accounting treatment (capex vs opex).
6. PO Issuance and Receipt of Goods/Services.

Approval Thresholds (signature authority)

- Up to $10k: Direct manager approval.
- $10k–$50k: Department head approval.
- $50k–$250k: Procurement + Finance approval.
- >$250k or multi-year commitments: Procurement + Finance + VP-level approval.
- Contracts involving >$1M, unusual indemnities, or regulatory clauses: require CFO and GC sign-off.

Vendor Selection and Due Diligence

- For vendors handling customer data or service continuity (e.g., cloud, logs, storage), complete a Security & Privacy Questionnaire and obtain Security Team sign-off before contracting.
- For material vendors (> $250k TCV), require 3 bids or documented sole-source rationale.

Contract Review and Standard Clauses

Legal maintains a Contract Playbook with preferred templates: SOW, Master Services Agreement (MSA), Data Processing Agreement (DPA), Reseller Agreement. Deviations from template must be tracked in Contract Deviation Log and require GC approval. Key negotiation guardrails:

- Liability cap: default to the contract value or statutory minimums.
- Indemnities: limited and mutual where possible.
- Data security: insert DPA and ISO/ SOC references for vendors processing customer data.
- IP assignment: ensure Redwood retains ownership of internal deliverables; customer-commissioned work to follow agreed SOW terms.

Contract Execution

- Electronic signature via approved vendor (DocuSign) is acceptable when signatory authority is documented.
- All executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository within 3 business days of signature.

Part C — Revenue Recognition & Billing

Principles and Policy (ASC 606 aligned)

Revenue is recognized based on the satisfaction of performance obligations and the transfer of control to the customer. The Finance team maintains detailed contract-level revenue schedules and defers amounts when performance obligations remain unmet.

Contract Intake and Revenue Assessment

1. Sales must submit the fully executed MSA + SOW + pricing schedule to Revenue Ops within 5 business days of signature.
2. Revenue Ops completes a contract review checklist for revenue accounting items: term, renewal mechanics, service performance obligations, variable consideration (credits, rebates), and payment terms.

Billing and Invoicing

- Standard hosted API usage: monthly invoicing in arrears with net-30 payment terms by default. Exceptions (prepay, usage commitments) must be approved by Revenue Ops/Finance.
- Dedicated/Private: May use milestone billing tied to delivery or recurring monthly/quarterly invoices per contract.
- Billing disputes must be submitted within 30 days of invoice date. Disputes do not negate payment obligations unless agreed in writing by Finance.

Deferred Revenue and Recognition Schedules

- Revenue Ops maintains a deferred revenue schedule by contract and ensures journal entries are posted by month-end close.
- Variable consideration: estimate using expected value/probability-weighted approach and update monthly. Adjustments are recorded in the period when information becomes available.

Credits, Refunds, and Refund Reserve

- Standard refund/credit terms are defined in the MSA. Ad hoc credits require Finance approval and must be logged in the Credit Log.
- Material refunds (> $50k) require VP Finance approval and Legal review.

Month-End Closing Controls

- All contracts signed within the month must be included in the month-end contract intake report.
- Revenue reconcilers (Revenue Ops + Accounting) must sign off reconciling items > $5k.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Revenue Ops (Owner): Contract intake, revenue schedules, billing operations, dispute triage.
- Accounting (Owner): Month-end journal entries, deferred revenue, audit support.
- Sales/AMs (Requestors): Timely submission of executed contracts and commercial changes.
- Legal: Contract language, risk assessment, and signature authority verification.

Controls, Audit, and Reporting

- All material contracts (> $250k TCV) will be reviewed quarterly by Finance and Legal for revenue recognition risk.
- Internal audit reviews procurement and revenue processes annually; results shared with the Audit Committee.
- Key reports: monthly revenue summary, deferred revenue aging, top 20 customer concentrations, procurement spend by vendor.

Exceptions and Escalations

- Exceptions to approval thresholds or contract templates must be documented and approved by GC and CFO.
- Escalation path for high-risk contracts: Account Executive -> Sales Leader -> Legal -> VP Finance -> CFO/GC.

Appendices and Templates

- Required templates: BudgetTemplate_YYYY.xlsx, PurchaseRequisition_Form.pdf, Contract Intake Checklist.xlsx, Standard MSA (v3.1), DPA (v2.0).
- Contract Deviation Log: link to Contract Repository.
- Sample GL coding guidance table: included below for common spend categories.

Sample GL Coding Table (text)

- 5000: Hosting (cloud compute)
- 5200: Third-party services (consulting)
- 5400: Software subscriptions (SaaS)
- 6100: Capital equipment
- 7000: Revenue - Hosted API

Change Management and Review Cycle

- This policy will be reviewed annually by Finance & Legal. Minor updates (non-policy changes) may be issued quarterly. Significant accounting or legal changes will trigger an immediate policy revision.

Contacts and Escalation List

- Finance (budgeting & forecasting): finance@redwoodinference.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwoodinference.com
- Revenue Ops & Billing: revenue-ops@redwoodinference.com
- Legal / Contracts: legal@redwoodinference.com

Revision History
